title: Choose the look for Shuttle Live
question: The roll assigned Shuttle Tube. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Shuttle Tube
options.lineage: feather-shuttle tubes: navy card, cork, speed bands
options.thesis: Each rally fills like a tube of shuttles, labelled the way a tube is: by speed.
options.viewport: Camera on top; a navy band carries the last shot in huge white type; far and near players mirrored below with the rally tube on the edge.
options.risk: Reads like racket-shop packaging if the bands turn decorative; navy panels take a slice of the camera view.

raised.raise: Total contrast: live numbers only in feather white on navy, never grey.
Nothing vanishes: a hit shows as HIT and stamps into its shot type when the reply lands.
Court map draws each shot as one straight stroke, newest brightest, labels fixed-size.
Far and near panels at identical scale on one shared baseline, mirrored.
One reversed plate per screen: the last shot's name and speed.

options.label: Umpire Flip Scoreboard
options.lineage: the flip-card scoreboard on the umpire's stand
options.thesis: Every number you need on flip cards you can read from the far baseline.
options.viewport: Camera on top; two big card panels (far, near) with the shot count huge and a row of small cards per shot type.
options.risk: The most familiar choice, and a scoreboard implies a score the app cannot keep.

options.label: Court Grid Numerals
options.thesis: The court's line grid becomes the construction grid; numbers are built cell by cell.
options.viewport: Camera on top; a court-green sheet with a faint grid and monumental cell-built shot counts.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads from the far baseline; loses on recognition, players do not know Crouwel.
options.risk: Grid-built numerals cost real build effort and can tip into poster over tool.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Shots as barcode columns strobing in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A barcode field of hits under the camera.
options.case: Loses both axes: strobing fights a glance and players do not see themselves in it.
options.kept: Total contrast for every live number.
options.risk: Strobing is hostile on a courtside screen.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each rally a coupon book torn off leg by leg.
options.viewport: Rally coupons stacked under the camera.
options.case: Loses both axes: travel paperwork says nothing about badminton.
options.kept: Nothing disappears; states stamp in place.
options.risk: Paper ephemera at a distance is unreadable.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Shots as transit lines between hit stations.
options.viewport: A court drawn as a line diagram.
options.case: Loses both axes: a rally is not a route network.
options.kept: Disciplined straight strokes with fixed-size labels on the court map.
options.risk: Turns a court into a subway map.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: A rally as plates at one fixed scale.
options.case: Loses both axes: cream editorial plates cannot be read from the court.
options.kept: Identical scale and baseline for both players.
options.risk: Cream and hairlines vanish at distance.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight and reversal.
options.viewport: A raked rack of stat slides.
options.case: Loses both axes: one type size cannot carry a glance from 10 metres.
options.kept: One reversed plate per screen for the single most important number.
options.risk: Raked panels fight a quick read.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What sports and fitness trackers ship: dark stat tiles with one neon accent.
canonCard.viewport: Camera on top, a grid of small dark tiles below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every workout app, and tiles too small to read from the court.
